record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.context_brief: Hamiltonian cycles in segment visibility graphs
record.original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, find a Hamiltonian cycle of G in polynomial time.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15 Given a segment visibility graph G in adjacency matrix form, identify a Hamiltonian cycle in G in polynomial time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S be a finite set of pairwise disjoint (non-crossing) closed line segments in the Euclidean plane, and let V be the set of the 2|S| endpoints of these segments. The segment endpoint visibility graph G = (V, E) has vertex set V, and two vertices u, v ∈ V are adjacent in G if and only if either (i) {u, v} are the two endpoints of a common segment in S, or (ii) the open straight-line segment from u to v does not meet (intersect) the interior of any segment of S. A Hamiltonian cycle of G is a cyclic ordering of V such that every consecutive pair (including the pair closing the cycle) is an edge of G.

It is known that, provided not all segments of S are collinear, such a graph G always admits a Hamiltonian cycle. The problem is the algorithmic question:

Given only the adjacency matrix of a segment endpoint visibility graph G (with no accompanying geometric realization of S), design an algorithm that outputs a Hamiltonian cycle of G and runs in time polynomial in |V|. Either provide such a polynomial-time algorithm or prove that none exists (e.g., establish hardness).
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of a Hamiltonian cycle in segment endpoint visibility graphs (when not all segments are collinear) was established by Hoffmann and Tóth, settling Mirzaian's conjecture. However, those proofs use the underlying geometric segment configuration. The algorithmic question of constructing a Hamiltonian cycle from only the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph in polynomial time does not appear to be resolved; recognition/reconstruction of segment visibility graphs is itself only known to lie in PSPACE (∃R), and no polynomial-time algorithm for finding such a Hamiltonian cycle from the adjacency matrix has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Segment Endpoint Visibility Graphs are Hamiltonian
status_evidence.snippet: Segment endpoint visibility graphs of any finite set of disjoint line segments in the plane admit a simple Hamiltonian polygon, provided not all segments are collinear.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of Hamiltonian cycles is established geometrically, but not from adjacency-matrix input.

status_evidence.title: Computational Complexity Aspects of Point Visibility Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recognition/reconstruction problems for visibility graphs lie in the existential theory of the reals; not known to be in NP.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic recognition/reconstruction complexity for visibility graphs remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Computing Boundary Cycle of a Pseudo-Triangle Polygon from its Visibility Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm for the special case of pseudo-triangle polygon visibility graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases have polynomial-time Hamiltonian cycle algorithms from the visibility graph alone.
